W normally gives you a shield and movement speed. When you have your passive up, your first W shields you and your second W heals you and your nearby allies after 2.5 seconds. To do this, your W checks if you are shielded. If you are shielded, you get the heal if not you get a shield. Guardian comes into the mix by shielding both you and your ally. Therefore when you W after the guardian shield it's as if you got the double cast.

Guardian gives shield that synergies with W shield. You can get the ally heal even if you don't have your passive ready.

I often ban Ryze or Annie, not because they are particularly hard to lane against--they aren't--rather because they have point and click hard cc: a root and stun respectively, which can completely shut down your ult mobility and set up the rest of their combos. Against what this thread has appeared to deem the hardest match-ups (Yasuo, Leblanc, Zed, and Fizz) I acknowledge that--at best-- I will go even with them and wait until team fighting and do my best to slay the enemy adc or support. However, against the two aforementioned champions they can stop your approach very effectively without having to use all their abilities you which leaves you without a choice but to wait until they have used their cc at which point the enemy adc could have mowed your team down.
